chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Gig pay and where club dates were played
summary: Gigs paid twenty-five to forty dollars a night; they discuss hotels, weddings and New Jersey weekend dates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well --
If you had a day job or a little job working and you could gig one or two gigs, you could make a pretty good salary for that week, you know.
Well some of the --
Twenty-five dollars, thirty dollars a night. They went (Inaudible) up to thirty-five, some of the things started going up.
Some of these gigs started paying like thirty dollars a night, or twenty dollars a night, or twenty-five dollars a night, you know, according to where you played at.

With the Savoy Sultans?
No. The Savoy Sultans worked mostly the Savoy. They didn't gig too much. They worked year round at the Savoy.

They was all -- when they wasn't working, they were playing out, you know -- They did some gigging, but most of their time they played at the Savoy. If they didn't work, they were working some place, another ballroom (unintelligible) or something like that.
